title: In A Grove

speaker_display.monk: the traveling monk who met the couple the day before
speaker_display.narrator: the outside narrator who only introduces who is speaking
speaker_display.woodcutter: the woodcutter who found the body

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he reports when he found the body.
items.scene: He tells the authorities that he found the body in the bushes that morning.
evidence: "I found him in the bushes this morning,"
the woodcutter said.

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he gives a factual account of the body's condition and nearby signs.
items.scene: He describes the body and what he found near it after locating it by the mountain road.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows his report of finding the body with details about its condition and the scene.
evidence: "The blood was already dry when I saw him."
"Broken bamboo and marks on the ground showed a fight."

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he reports seeing the couple the previous day.
items.scene: He speaks after the woodcutter describes finding the body, giving his account of the previous day.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds that he saw the couple yesterday, after the woodcutter's account of finding the body.
evidence: "I saw the couple yesterday at noon,"
the traveling monk said.

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he adds what the man carried and who rode beside him.
items.scene: He continues his account of seeing the couple the day before.
items.reaction_to_previous: He elaborates on seeing the couple by describing the man's weapons and his wife's place beside him.
evidence: "He carried a sword and bow, and his wife rode beside him."
"I saw the couple yesterday at noon,"

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he reports that he caught the bandit.
items.scene: He tells the others he caught Tajomaru near the bridge.
items.reaction_to_previous: He shifts from the monk's account of the couple to reporting the bandit's capture.
evidence: "I caught the famous bandit Tajomaru near the bridge,"
the constable said.

items.speaker_state: Matter-of-fact, giving details about the captured man's condition and directing the search for the wife.
items.scene: After reporting Tajomaru's capture, he describes the man's fall and bow, then instructs others to find the wife.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows the report of the capture with details and an instruction to ask the wife what happened.
evidence: "He had fallen off a horse, but still had Takehiro's bow."
"Find the wife and ask her what he did."

items.speaker_state: Neutral; she identifies Takehiro and his relationship to her daughter.
items.scene: The old woman speaks after the constable says to find the wife and ask her what happened.
items.reaction_to_previous: She responds to the search for the wife by identifying Takehiro as her daughter's husband.
evidence: "Takehiro, a kind samurai, married my daughter Masago,"
the old woman said.

items.speaker_state: Worried and pleading for news of her daughter.
items.scene: The old woman asks that her daughter be found before she is sent home without news.
items.reaction_to_previous: She adds an urgent request after identifying Masago as her daughter and describing her.
evidence: "Please find her before you send me home without news."
"She is proud and only nineteen."

items.speaker_state: Matter-of-fact, claiming that the killing was fair.
items.scene: Tajomaru answers during his account of the events involving the couple.
items.reaction_to_previous: He presents his claim about the killing after the old woman's request to find her daughter.
evidence: "I killed him fairly,"
"Twenty-three blows—no other man had lasted twenty!"

items.speaker_state: Confident in his account of the fight and what followed.
items.scene: Tajomaru continues his account, describing the wife's plea, the sword fight, and his departure.
items.reaction_to_previous: He explains what he means by saying he killed Takehiro fairly.
evidence: "I freed him for a fair sword fight."
"Twenty-three blows—no other man had lasted twenty!"

items.speaker_state: Neutral; she begins recounting what she did after the bandit left.
items.scene: Masago speaks at the temple about approaching her husband after the bandit left him tied up.
items.reaction_to_previous: She gives her own account after Tajomaru has described his version of the events.
evidence: "I crawled towards my husband,"
"The bandit had left him tied up."

items.speaker_state: Ashamed and uncertain about where she can go after her failed attempt to drown herself.
items.scene: Masago continues her account, describing her failed attempt to drown herself and asking what future remains for her.
evidence: "I later tried drowning myself, but I failed."
"Where can I go after that?"
'Kill me,' he said, so I stabbed him. I could not stand those eyes.

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he recounts hearing the bandit speak kindly to Masago.
items.scene: Takehiro's spirit speaks through a medium about what he heard.
items.reaction_to_previous: He begins his account after Masago describes her failed attempt to drown herself.
evidence: "I heard him speaking kindly to her,"
Takehiro's spirit said through a medium.

items.speaker_state: Neutral; he describes dying and not returning.
items.scene: Takehiro's spirit concludes his account of what happened after he was stabbed.
evidence: "I sank into the darkness and never came back."
"Someone came slowly towards me on silent feet."
